chunks: But did not add: "If God may please."

key_terms.يَسْتَثْنُونَ: to add a condition (specifically 'if God wills')

ai.seo_question: Why did the people of the Garden not say 'if God wills' when speaking to the people of the Fire?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the phrase 'wa la yastathnuun' (and they do not make exceptions) in Surah Al-Qalam is interpreted as the denial of any intercession or reprieve for the inhabitants of the Fire, reinforcing the concept of divine justice where deeds are weighed without arbitrary mercy. This highlights the finality of the Hereafter, contrasting with the conditional 'in sha' Allah' often used in worldly matters to acknowledge God's will, thereby underscoring the certainty of the separation between the righteous and the wicked.
